added.d: Its contained survival premise, clear outbreak rules, social conflict, and moral stakes fit his strong response to serious heightened thrillers like Alice in Borderland and Squid Game. The moderate romance and occasional melodramatic or action-heavy moments keep it below his courtroom and grounded justice favorites, but its 12-episode length and sincere emotional core are an excellent fit.

Its supernatural mystery is emotionally sincere and rule-driven enough to fit his tolerance for heightened premises, though it is less grounded and less justice-focused than his strongest favorites. The eight-episode format and serious atmosphere fit well, but the reported loss of investment toward the ending lowers confidence in its depth and narrative tightness.

Little Women has a serious crime-mystery setup with family corruption, hidden motives, and escalating stakes, so it can fit his appetite for moral conflict and plot weight. But it is more stylish and melodramatic than his top courtroom/puzzle-driven favorites, and the action-mystery energy may feel closer to the exaggerated side he rejected in Vincenzo than to his grounded legal and revenge picks.
